en.name: Pius IV
en.summary: The pope who brought the long-running Council of Trent to its final close in 1563, sealing the Catholic Church's Counter-Reformation program.
en.body: Giovanni Angelo Medici reconvened and successfully concluded the Council of Trent after decades of interruption, securing agreement on the doctrinal and disciplinary reforms that would define Catholic identity for the next four centuries. He balanced this achievement with a notably more moderate temperament than his predecessor Paul IV, easing some of the harsher policies of the preceding pontificate.
